After an unusually long three-week wait, new beta updates are now starting to roll out to developers, including iPadOS 27 beta 5 and several other versions. Here are the details.

iPadOS 27 beta 5 and more Apple updates have been released

With iOS 27 public release still about a month or so away, it typically signals that the beta release cycle is about to pick up pace.

Apple today officially released several beta 5 versions, including iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27.

Right now, only developers can download and install these new updates. However, if Apple follows its usual practice, the public beta versions of the same software should be available within a day or two.

At this stage of the beta cycle, we don't expect to find major user-visible changes in Apple's software. Instead, August is usually when two main things happen with Apple betas:

  • New betas are released more frequently, typically weekly, but with fewer visible changes
  • Apple's focus shifts to bug fixes and performance improvements

Apple has emphasized that new operating systems like iOS 27 will deliver performance improvements over the previous generation.

Although this has been the case to some extent during the beta phase, you can expect Apple's new software to run more smoothly with beta 5 and over the coming weeks, with more bugs fixed.

That said, if there really are any new features or notable changes in this update, we'll let you know.

Have you spotted anything new in iPadOS 27 beta 5 or any of the other versions? Feel free to share in the comments.
